statement: You are given an array of integers nums and an integer k. A subarray, a contiguous piece of nums, is nice if it contains exactly k odd numbers.
Return the number of nice subarrays.
Only whether each number is odd matters, so this is the binary-subarray count in disguise. A sliding window counts subarrays with at most x odd numbers, and the answer is atMost(k) − atMost(k − 1).

examples.explanation: Only [1, 1, 2, 1] and [1, 2, 1, 1] contain exactly three odd numbers.
A nice subarray must contain both 1s. It can start anywhere from index 0 to 3 (4 choices) and end anywhere from index 6 to 9 (4 choices), giving 4 × 4 = 16.
